ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Mary McLeod Bethune

code.originalText: Diagnosis visit: spirometry, FeNO and echocardiogram results with the pulmonology consultation; asthma confirmed, heart failure excluded, hypertensive heart disease found; start of budesonide-formoterol as maintenance and reliever

text.paragraph: Diagnosis visit: lung function, FeNO and echocardiogram results with the pulmonology consultation. [S]

Mrs. Bethune returns two weeks after her first visit. This morning she had spirometry before and after albuterol, a diffusion test and FeNO in the pulmonary function laboratory, and an echocardiogram, and she then saw Dr. Oyelowo-Brandt. Her symptoms are unchanged: she wakes with cough and a tight chest two or three nights a week and is breathless on one flight of stairs; she has used albuterol most days. Her home blood pressure readings over the week averaged 144/84. She has heartburn two or three evenings a week and a blocked nose most days. She asks plainly whether this is asthma, her heart or her weight. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-03-23; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Dignified and composed; speaks in full sentences; weight 87.6 kg; blood pressure 146/86, pulse 78; oxygen saturation 96 percent
Fundoscopy: mild arteriolar narrowing; no hemorrhages or exudates
Swollen, pale inferior turbinates; no polyps visible by anterior rhinoscopy
Scattered expiratory wheeze on forced expiration; no crackles
Regular rhythm; no murmur or gallop; jugular venous pressure not raised; no edema; foot pulses present

Wheeze, cough and breathlessness for four months: waking with cough and tight chest two or three nights a week, breathless on one flight of stairs, relieved by albuterol, worse with colds, dust and strong scents; known asthma for many years but never confirmed by lung function testing and never treated with an inhaled steroid. Asthma, COPD and heart failure to be distinguished: spirometry with bronchodilator response, FeNO and an echocardiogram booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented chronic asthma. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Blocked nose, thick postnasal drip and a reduced sense of smell for years, worse in the last year; no nosebleeds; never seen by an ear, nose and throat specialist
S — Synthetic upper-airway symptoms; superseded by the diagnosis of chronic rhinosinusitis after nasal endoscopy.
Gastro-esophageal reflux: heartburn and an acid taste two or three evenings a week, worse after late meals and lying down; no trouble swallowing, vomiting, black stools or weight loss
S — Synthetic comorbidity of asthma; not a claim about her real health.
Obesity, class 1 (BMI 33.1); she wants to walk more and to keep up with her work, and agreed to talk about it
S — Synthetic comorbidity recorded in her words and with her agreement; not a claim about her real weight.

Asthma, confirmed: variable airflow obstruction (FEV1 64 percent predicted, rising 270 mL or 21 percent after bronchodilator, with a normal post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC of 0.72 and normal DLCO); type 2 inflammation (FeNO 46 ppb, blood eosinophils 0.42 x10^3/uL, total IgE 210, house dust mite sensitization); not COPD and not heart failure. Uncontrolled at diagnosis on albuterol alone
S — Synthetic modern confirmation linked to her documented chronic asthma.

Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure: clinic blood pressure 152/88 and 146/86, home average 144/84; mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with grade 1 diastolic dysfunction and a normal ejection fraction (62 percent); BNP 48 pg/mL
S — Synthetic finding of the modern work-up; not a claim about her real heart.
Hyperlipidemia: LDL cholesterol 144 mg/dL; 10-year ASCVD risk above 20 percent with hypertension

value.displayName: Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure

list.item:
Asthma, confirmed, uncontrolled (J45.40). Asthma confirmed: FEV1 rose 270 mL (21 percent) after albuterol, and the post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC of 0.72 shows no persistent obstruction, so this is not COPD; DLCO is normal; FeNO 46 ppb and blood eosinophils of 0.42 show type 2 inflammation. The results were read with race-neutral equations: with older race-based equations her FEV1 would have looked closer to normal. Her asthma is uncontrolled (Asthma Control Test 14), and albuterol alone is the riskiest way to treat it. Dr. Oyelowo-Brandt and I agree on GINA track 1. [S]
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg: one inhalation twice daily and one as needed, up to 12 a day; albuterol stopped.
Inhaler technique taught and checked today.
Written asthma action plan with peak flow zones; peak flow meter given.
Pneumococcal vaccine today.

Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure (I11.9). Her breathlessness is not from heart failure: BNP 48, ejection fraction 62 percent, no fluid on the chest X-ray and a normal jugular venous pressure. But the echocardiogram and ECG show mild left ventricular hypertrophy from untreated high blood pressure (clinic 146/86, home 144/84), so her heart needs protecting. [S]
Amlodipine 5 mg daily; no beta-blocker because of asthma.
Lower-salt diet; home readings to continue.
Potassium and kidney function at the next visit.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). LDL 144 mg/dL with hypertension and prediabetes: 10-year ASCVD risk above 20 percent. [S]
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Lipid panel in six weeks.

Chronic nasal symptoms (R09.81). Years of blockage, postnasal drip and reduced smell with swollen turbinates: chronic rhinosinusitis is likely and worsens asthma. [S]
Fluticasone nasal spray and saline.
Ear, nose and throat review with nasal endoscopy in four weeks.

Gastro-esophageal reflux (K21.9). Symptomatic reflux, treated for its own sake. [S]
Omeprazole 20 mg daily for eight weeks.
No food for three hours before bed; head of the bed raised.

Obesity, class 1 (E66.811). Her breathlessness is from asthma, not her weight, and she was told so; she would like help to walk more. [S]
Dietitian visit as she wishes.
A walking plan once her breathing settles.

Wheeze, cough and breathlessness (R06.2). Explained by the diagnosis made today; superseded. [S]
Problem resolved.

Follow-up: Six-week review. Ear, nose and throat in four weeks. Follow the action plan: two extra inhalations and a call to the clinic if in the yellow zone for more than a day; emergency care in the red zone. Next scheduled visit 2026-05-04: six-week asthma review: control, inhaler technique and adherence, the ear, nose and throat result, blood pressure and reflux. [S]
